planting.note: Surface-sow the fine seed and press it into contact with moist soil rather than burying it, since light aids germination in this self-seeding annual.

directions: Bona is a European field cultivar of German chamomile selected for a heavier, more uniform flush of flower heads than unselected seed-grown populations, making it a common choice in commercial chamomile tea production. Direct-sow in early spring as soon as the soil can be worked, scattering the tiny seeds onto a fine, weed-free seedbed and tamping them lightly without covering them, since they need light to sprout. Thin seedlings to stand several inches apart once true leaves appear, and keep the bed evenly moist but not waterlogged through germination and early growth. Harvest the daisy-like flower heads every few days once the white petals have fully reflexed downward, drying them promptly on screens out of direct sun to preserve color and aroma for tea.
